source_documents.title: Balancing the reverse intersystem crossing and radiative decay via meta- substitution of selenium in multi-resonance emitters for efficient organic light emitting diodes

reference_evidence_units.quote: By introducing selenium at the meta-position relative to the boron atom, the emitter DBNOSe achieves a unique balance between enhanced reverse intersystem crossing and preserved radiative decay.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DBNOSe
reference_evidence_units.statement: Faster rISC while keeping a high kr.

reference_evidence_units.quote: DBNOSe exhibits a markedly accelerated RISC rate of 1.35 × 106 s− 1 while maintaining a high radiative efficiency
reference_evidence_units.subject: DBNOSe

reference_evidence_units.quote: In contrast, ortho-substitution leads to excessive selenium participation that suppresses kr, whereas para-substitution results in insufficient SOC enhancement and subopti mal kRISC.
reference_evidence_units.subject: ortho/para analogues
reference_evidence_units.statement: Position of Se trades kr against kRISC.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Analogues not all characterised in this paper.
